easy.explanation: Gideon pitched beside the well of Harod.
Three hundred men lapped the water and remained.
easy.q: How many men remained after the drinking test?

answers: Those who were fearful and afraid
easy.explanation: The fearful and afraid were told to depart.
easy.q: Who was first told to return home?

answers: So Israel would not boast that its own hand had saved it
So the army could cross the Jordan quickly

medium.q: Why did the Lord reduce Gideon's army?

answers: They lapped with their tongues, putting a hand to their mouths
medium.explanation: The three hundred lapped water with their hands to their mouths.
medium.q: How did the three hundred men drink?
What does the word “victuals” mean in verse 8?

answers: It showed that the victory was not gained by Israel's numbers
It allowed Midian to join Israel
challenge.explanation: The small army prevented Israel from claiming the victory for itself.
challenge.q: What was the connection between reducing the army and the victory?

answers: The drinking test, sending away the fearful, keeping three hundred
Sending away the fearful, testing the drinking, keeping three hundred
Keeping three hundred, sending away the fearful, testing the drinking

The Lord wanted a larger army

paragraphs.title: The Dream in the Midianite Camp

easy.explanation: Gideon went down with Phurah his servant.
easy.q: Who went down with Gideon to the edge of the camp?

answers: A cake of barley bread that overturned a tent
A large army on a hill
easy.explanation: A barley cake struck and overturned a tent.
easy.q: What did the man see in his dream?

answers: He worshipped and returned to the host of Israel
easy.explanation: Gideon worshipped, returned, and encouraged his men.
easy.q: How did Gideon respond after hearing the dream and its interpretation?

answers: The sword of Gideon and the fall of Midian
The return of the fearful men
medium.explanation: He interpreted the barley cake as Gideon's sword and Midian's defeat.
medium.q: What did the fellow say the dream represented?

answers: To hear what the Midianites said and be strengthened
medium.explanation: Hearing the dream and its interpretation would strengthen Gideon.
medium.q: Why did the Lord tell Gideon to go down with Phurah?

answers: The meaning or explanation of the dream
medium.explanation: It means the explanation of what the dream signified.
medium.q: What does “the interpretation thereof” refer to?

answers: A Midianite himself foretold the fall of his own camp
Gideon saw the whole army flee
challenge.explanation: The dream and its interpretation came from within the enemy camp.
challenge.q: Why did the dream strengthen Gideon?

answers: The sword of Gideon and Israel's victory
The large size of Midian's army
The return of the fearful men
challenge.explanation: The fellow identified it with Gideon's sword.
challenge.q: What did the barley cake symbolize?

answers: He moved from fear to worship, encouragement, and action
challenge.explanation: Gideon worshipped and told his men to arise because the Lord had delivered Midian.
challenge.q: What change occurred in Gideon after hearing the dream?

easy.explanation: Gideon divided them into three companies.
easy.q: Into how many companies did Gideon divide the three hundred men?

answers: A trumpet, an empty pitcher, and a lamp
easy.explanation: Each man carried a trumpet, pitcher, and lamp.
Gideon said, “Look on me, and do likewise.”
easy.q: Whose actions were the soldiers to imitate?

answers: Blow their trumpets and cry the battle shout
medium.explanation: They were to blow their trumpets around the camp and shout.
medium.q: What were the men to do when Gideon blew a trumpet?

answers: So they would be hidden at first
So they could be used to carry water
So they could mark the Jordan
medium.explanation: The pitchers concealed the lamps until the attack began.
medium.q: Why were the lamps placed inside the pitchers?

medium.explanation: The three hundred were divided into three groups.
medium.q: What does “companies” mean in this context?

answers: The lamps were hidden in pitchers and revealed when the pitchers were broken
The trumpets were hidden while the pitchers were displayed
The soldiers hid while the lamps were extinguished
challenge.explanation: The pitchers concealed the lamps until they were broken.
challenge.q: How did the plan combine concealment and revelation?

answers: It attributed the victory to the Lord and Gideon
challenge.explanation: The cry was, “The sword of the Lord, and of Gideon.”
challenge.q: What was the meaning of the battle cry?

answers: He led by example and required coordinated action
He left each man to act alone
He wanted the soldiers to wait for Midian
challenge.explanation: Gideon would act first, and the men were to follow his example.
challenge.q: What does Gideon's command, “Look on me, and do likewise,” show?

answers: At the beginning of the day
In the beginning of the middle watch
easy.explanation: Gideon came at the beginning of the middle watch.
They brake the pitchers in their hands.
easy.q: What did the soldiers do to the pitchers?

easy.explanation: The host ran, cried, and fled.
easy.q: What happened to the host of Midian?

answers: They blew trumpets, broke pitchers, and revealed the lamps
They broke pitchers, returned to camp, and extinguished lamps
They revealed lamps, crossed the Jordan, and waited
medium.explanation: The three companies followed this sequence during the attack.
medium.q: Which sequence describes the soldiers' actions?

answers: The Lord set every man's sword against his fellow
Israel shot arrows from the hills
medium.explanation: The Lord caused the Midianites to strike one another.
medium.q: How was the Midianite camp harmed from within?

answers: A division or watch during the night
medium.explanation: It describes a night watch during which the attack began.
medium.q: What does “the middle watch” refer to?

answers: Trumpets, lights, and surrounding positions created the impression of attack from every side
A large army crossed the Jordan
All the tribes of Israel arrived at once
challenge.explanation: The sounds and lights around the camp created confusion and fear.
challenge.q: Why could the attack make the force seem larger than three hundred men?

answers: Breaking them revealed the lamps and increased the panic
Breaking them blocked the Jordan crossings
Breaking them told Israel to return
challenge.explanation: The lamps had been hidden until the pitchers were broken.
challenge.q: What was the connection between breaking the pitchers and the flight?

answers: The camp collapsed in confusion rather than retreating in order
challenge.explanation: The host ran, cried, fled, and even fought among itself.
challenge.q: What does the description of the camp's flight emphasize?

easy.explanation: Men from Naphtali, Asher, and Manasseh joined the pursuit.
easy.q: Which tribes were gathered to pursue Midian?

answers: To the children of the east
easy.explanation: Gideon sent messengers throughout Mount Ephraim.
easy.q: To whom did Gideon send messengers?

answers: The waters unto Beth-barah and Jordan
easy.explanation: They were told to take the waters and the Jordan crossings.

answers: To join the pursuit of the fleeing Midianites
medium.explanation: The tribes were called to continue pursuing Midian.

answers: It would block possible routes of escape

answers: Places where people can pass over

answers: The initial victory led to a broader pursuit

challenge.q: What does the move from three hundred men to additional tribes show?

answers: They were routes by which the fleeing army could travel
The drinking test was held there
challenge.explanation: Controlling those places could prevent escape.
challenge.q: Why was it important to seize the waters and the Jordan?

answers: Both were coordinated steps in continuing the pursuit
The first called for surrender and the second for peace
challenge.explanation: Gideon summoned support and arranged to block escape routes.
challenge.q: What connection exists between calling the tribes and sending messengers to Ephraim?

easy.explanation: The Israelites captured Oreb and Zeeb.
They were two princes of Midian.
easy.q: What was the position of Oreb and Zeeb?

easy.explanation: Their heads were brought to Gideon on the other side of Jordan.
easy.q: To whom were their heads brought?

medium.explanation: Oreb was slain upon the rock Oreb.
Zeeb was slain at the winepress of Zeeb.

medium.q: What does “princes” mean in “two princes of Midian”?

The names existed before the pursuit

It caused Gideon to release Midian
